title: Production Launch: Security Authorization Guidance
content:
Purpose:
This runbook defines the minimum security authorization criteria, evidence collection automation, and exception approval process required for a production launch at Redwood Inference. It is focused on four cross-cutting controls: RBAC v2 alignment, audit-log schema and tamper-resistance, automated evidence artifacts in CI/CD, and SIEM export/alerting mappings.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: release owners, engineering leads, security reviewers, SREs, and compliance reviewers.
- Scope: Hosted API and Dedicated release paths; private deployments should follow the same checklist with additional infra controls (VPC, KMS HSM).

Prerequisites before security review:
1) Master release ticket exists and references relevant feature flags and deployment targets (Jira key on linked artifacts).
2) All infra IaC and deployment manifests pushed to review branch; PR links attached in release ticket.
3) Automated test pipeline runs (unit, integration, infra validation) with successful artifacts stored in CI artifact registry.

Pre-release security checklist (minimum):
- RBAC v2 role review:
  * Confirm roles map to least-privilege personas. Provide a short justification for any role with more than 10 permissions.
  * Verify service-to-service roles are scoped by audience and purpose (no wildcard resource grants).
  * Ensure any new admin-level roles have a named owner and rotation cadence documented.
  * Check temporal/just-in-time elevation plans (if used) and approval TTL.
- Audit log schema verification:
  * Confirm events include: timestamp (ISO8601), user_id, service, resource_id, action, request_id/correlation_id, outcome (success/fail), client_ip, region, and optional session metadata.
  * Ensure log entries include an immutable sequence id and are stored to write-once medium or append-only storage before transformation.
  * Verify retention policy (minimum prod retention: 365 days for security-critical logs) and deletion approvers.
- Evidence automation:
  * CI must produce an evidence bundle (signed manifest) containing: deployment manifest diff, RBAC diff, test-run hashes, artifact checksums, and audit export sample.
  * Evidence bundles should be uploaded to the secure evidence bucket (path format: /evidence/releases/<jira>-<yyyymmdd>-<sha>).
  * Automated attestations (CI job) must sign the bundle using the deployment pipeline key.
- SIEM export readiness:
  * Confirm forwarder configuration (syslog/HTTP) and field mappings to SIEM schema.
  * Provide sample event export and a mapping table (audit field -> SIEM field).
  * Pre-author alert rules for high-severity detections (privileged role change, failed auth bursts, unusual region access).

RBAC v2 specific checks (detailed):
- Role inheritance: list inherited permissions and justify any role that inherits more than 3 roles.
- Approval gates: developer pushes that modify role bindings must open an approval ticket automatically. Gate must block prod deploy without approval.
- Cross-tenant access: deny-by-default; any exception requires documented compensating control and rotation for access keys.

Audit log schema example (required fields):
- event_time: "2025-02-21T14:22:33Z"
- tenant_id: "t-12345"
- user_id: "u-maya"
- actor_type: "service|human|support-bot"
- request_id: "req-7f3a"
- action: "role.bind.update"
- resource_type: "policy|instance|model"
- resource_id: "model-xyz"
- outcome: "success|failure"
- src_ip: "34.23.45.6"
- seq_id: "000000012345"
(Teams must confirm any additional product-specific fields prior to sign-off.)

Evidence automation patterns (recommended):
- CI job names and artifact conventions: deploy-evidence, rbac-diff, audit-sample, siem-snapshot.
- Signed manifests: use pipeline signer key stored in KMS; manifest JSON must include artifact checksums and a hash-chain pointer to previous release evidence.
- Automated evidence verification: security reviewer can run a single script (./tools/verify-evidence.sh <bundle>) to validate signatures and checksums.

SIEM export and alert mappings (operational):
- Use structured JSON events; avoid freeform text in the top-level message field.
- Map: tenant_id -> sourcetype.tenant, user_id -> user.id, action -> event.action, outcome -> event.outcome, request_id -> event.id, seq_id -> event.sequence.
- Example pre-launch detection rules to configure:
  1) Privileged-binding-created: alert on action == "role.bind.create" where bound_role in admin_roles and origin != infra-approval-service.
  2) Failed-auth-burst: > 50 auth failures for same user_id in 10 minutes.

Launch sign-off template (to paste into release ticket):
- Security Reviewer: <name>
- Date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Checklist: RBAC v2 verified, Audit schema validated, Evidence bundle present and signed, SIEM export validated, Exception log is empty or approved.
- Sign-off decision: APPROVE | APPROVE WITH EXCEPTIONS | REJECT
- Comments: <freeform>

Exception approval workflow (when an item cannot meet criteria):
1) Author opens an exception request under the release ticket with fields: exception_id, scope, duration, compensating_controls, mitigation_plan, owner, risk_score.
2) Security triage within 48 hours. If approved, exception must be timeboxed and attached to the central exceptions ledger.
3) For high-risk exceptions (risk_score>7), require at least two approvers (security lead + product owner) and pre-release compensating controls (e.g., additional SIEM rules, read-only locks).
4) Automated reminders: exceptions near TTL expiration generate escalations to on-call and the release owner.

Post-launch monitoring and required postmortem evidence:
- 72-hour elevated monitoring window: collect SIEM dashboards and tokenized anomalies export; include these in post-launch evidence bundle.
- If any high-severity alerts trigger, pause rollout and open an incident with standard IR runbook attached.
- Postmortem must reference the evidence bundle path and list remediation items with owners and due dates.

Appendices (quick references):
A) Sample RBAC-binding snippet (YAML)
  apiVersion: rbac.redwood/v2
  kind: RoleBinding
  metadata:
    name: analytics-readonly-binding
  spec:
    role: roles/analytics.viewer
    members:
      - user:u-data-eng
      - service:svc-metrics

B) Minimal audit-log field table (CSV-friendly): field,description,required
  event_time,ISO8601 timestamp,yes
  tenant_id,customer tenant id,yes
  user_id,actor identifier,yes
  action,api or console action,yes
  resource_type,service resource type,yes
  resource_id,identifier for resource,yes
  outcome,success/failure,yes
  seq_id,append-only sequence id,yes

C) Example Jira exception template (copy into ticket description):
  [Exception] short summary
  - scope: (RBAC | infra | data-access)
  - intended duration: YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD
  - compensating controls: list
  - business justification: 1-2 sentences
  - approver(s): @security-lead @product-owner

D) Quick commands:
  - Verify evidence bundle: ./tools/verify-evidence.sh <bundle-path>
  - Export SIEM mapping sample: ./tools/siem-export-sample --release <jira> --out sample.json

Contact and escalation:
- Primary security reviewer: security-reviews@redwood.ai
- On-call security (pager): #sec-oncall (Slack) and PagerDuty escalation as configured in oncall rota.

Notes and open items (for this runbook iteration):
- Add template for signed attestations (v1) to the tools repo.
- Confirm retention SLA for audit logs across private deployments (KMS/HSM note).

End of runbook.
